title: Global Hiring Trends & Compensation Benchmarks 2025
excerpt: Key findings on salary expectations, remote working policies, and employee retention factors shaping the recruitment market this year.

author.name: Amara Okonkwo
author.bio: Amara leads SLEDMC's talent research desk, analyzing labor market data across mobility and skills corridors.

content.text: The 2025 hiring landscape is defined by tighter technical talent pools and rising candidate expectations around flexibility.
Remote work is now a baseline expectation
Organizations that fail to offer hybrid or remote options are seeing longer time-to-fill for mid-to-senior technical roles.
Salary transparency continues to shift negotiating power toward candidates, particularly in specialized engineering and healthcare fields.

title: Navigating Talent Shortages in Technical Sectors
excerpt: Strategies for organizations competing for rare software and engineering skills in a tight labor market.

author.name: David Mensah
author.bio: David specializes in technical and engineering recruitment across international placements.

content.text: Technical talent shortages are forcing employers to rethink sourcing strategy beyond traditional job boards.
Referral programs, international recruitment, and upskilling partnerships are proving more effective than passive listings.

title: CV Writing Tips for International Job Applications
excerpt: How candidates can tailor their CVs to stand out to recruiters and hiring managers across borders.

author.name: Farida Haddad
author.bio: Farida supports candidates through CV preparation, interview coaching, and international placement guidance.

content.text: A strong CV for international roles highlights transferable skills and quantifies impact clearly for reviewers unfamiliar with your home market.
Replace task lists with measurable results — numbers, percentages, and timeframes make achievements easy to scan.
